check.q: The madd in «وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ» before the shaddah is ...
check.why: Alif followed by a letter with shaddah (a permanent sukoon) in the word: madd lazim kalimi, 6.

practice.q: Map Al-Fatihah 1:4 «مَٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ» to the six families.
practice.a: مَٰلِكِ: small alif madd 2; يَوْمِ: و sakin after fathah (leen when stopping only); ٱلدِّينِ: sun letter د, madd 'arid at the stop.
practice.model: I do: مَٰلِكِ: small alif, natural madd 2. يَوْمِ: the waw is leen; we are not stopping, so no lengthening. ٱلدِّينِ: د is a sun letter; stopping: 'arid 2, 4 or 6.

practice.q: «لِلَّهِ»: the laam is ...

independent.model: The teacher maps تَبَٰرَكَ: small alif madd 2; ٱلَّذِى: sun letter laam.

independent.q: Extend: name the family you find hardest and one practice for it.
independent.a: Personal target with a practice plan.

independent.q: Stretch: explain the difference between madd lazim and madd 'arid.
independent.a: Lazim: permanent sukoon in the word, always 6; 'arid: sukoon only from stopping, 2, 4 or 6.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Kahf 18:1-5: hear, understand and memorise
lessons.bigQuestion: The Prophet ﷺ told us that memorising the first ten ayat of Al-Kahf protects from the Dajjal. Why might these ayat protect?
objectives: To memorise Al-Kahf 18:1-5 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: recite 18:1-5 after the teacher, word for word
Most: recite 18:1-5 from memory with no more than one prompt
Some: link 18:1-5 to the ayat before and name the tajweed rules in them
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: protection through firm belief and the Qur'an

hook.text: The Prophet ﷺ told us that memorising the first ten ayat of Al-Kahf protects from the Dajjal. Why might these ayat protect?
hook.a: They affirm the straight Book, the reward of believers and the warning against false claims about Allah: firm belief protects (18:1 to 5).

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever memorises ten ayat from the beginning of Surat Al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal' (Muslim). Allah says: 'All praise is due to Allah, who has sent down upon His Servant the Book and has not made therein any deviance' (Al-Kahf 18:1).

starter.q: Which surah begins «ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ...»?
Lahn khafi is ...
Saktah means ...

teach.heading: New ayat: Al-Kahf 18:1-5
bullets: Listen first: the teacher recites twice
Follow each word with your finger
teach.note: Begin with isti'adhah and Bismillah. Recite 18:1-5 slowly twice from the mushaf (spoken recitation only, no melody exercises), pointing to each word on the shared screen. The Arabic is the Qur'an in Uthmani script (Hafs 'an 'Asim, Madinah mushaf); check it against the school mushaf.

quote.text: ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَلَمْ يَجْعَل لَّهُۥ عِوَجَا ۜ (١) قَيِّمًۭا لِّيُنذِرَ بَأْسًۭا شَدِيدًۭا مِّن لَّدُنْهُ وَيُبَشِّرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا حَسَنًۭا (٢) مَّٰكِثِينَ فِيهِ أَبَدًۭا (٣) وَيُنذِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوا۟ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ وَلَدًۭا (٤) مَّا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍۢ وَلَا لِءَابَآئِهِمْ ۚ كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةًۭ تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَٰهِهِمْ ۚ إِن يَقُولُونَ إِلَّا كَذِبًۭا (٥)

teach.heading: What the ayat mean
bullets: This is a translation of the meaning, not the Qur'an itself
teach.note: Read the English slowly. Remind pupils: only the Arabic is the Qur'an; any English is a translation of its meaning (here Saheeh International).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: [All] praise is [due] to Allah, who has sent down upon His Servant the Book and has not made therein any deviance.
[He has made it] straight, to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward
In which they will remain forever
And to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."
They have no knowledge of it, nor had their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they speak not except a lie.

teach.heading: Tajweed spotlight in today's ayat
teach.note: Point to each word in the mushaf. Pupils say the rule before you do.

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: mics in turn
teach.note: Talaqqi (تلقي): learning recitation by hearing it from the teacher. Work through 18:1-5 one ayah at a time. Keep a visible order of names (the register) so every pupil gets a turn across the week. Unmute only the pupils whose turn it is; everyone else whispers along with mics muted.
cycle: Pupils listen, mics muted, eyes on the words
Mics on in turn: three pupils repeat in register order
Teacher corrects one point for each
Whole class repeats softly, then moves to the next ayah

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: The saktah after «عِوَجَا» in 18:1 means ...
options: A brief silent pause, no new breath
check.why: Saktah: a short pause without taking breath; it separates 'no deviance' from 'straight'.

practice.q: Chunk and link Al-Kahf 18:1-5 together, ayah by ayah.
practice.a: The class recites 18:1-5 together without the mushaf.
practice.model: I do: chunk 18:1-5. Ayah 1: 3 times looking, 3 times without looking. Then ayah 2 the same way. Then link: recite 1 and 2 together twice. Finish by reciting the whole chunk once without the mushaf.

practice.a: idgham without ghunnah

independent.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 18:1-5 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
independent.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
independent.model: The teacher shows the 3-3-link method once: read the ayah 3 times looking, say it 3 times without looking, then link it to the ayah before it. Rota: names on screen, about 90 seconds each, so every pupil is heard at least once a week; the teacher marks the rubric and gives one target.

independent.q: In the portal box, explain what 18:4 to 5 warn against.
independent.a: Saying that Allah has taken a son: a grave word without knowledge.

independent.q: Explain why the saktah protects the meaning of 18:1 to 2.
independent.a: Without it, قَيِّمًا could seem to describe 'deviance'; the pause makes clear 'straight' describes the Book.

exit.q: Al-Kahf 18:3: «مَّٰكِثِينَ ...» Which word comes next?
exit.a: فِيهِ

exit.q: Back to our ponder: The Prophet ﷺ told us that memorising the first ten ayat of Al-Kahf protects from the Dajjal. Why might these ayat protect?
exit.a: They affirm the straight Book, the reward of believers and the warning against false claims about Allah: firm belief protects (18:1 to 5).

keywords.def: humble presence of heart in prayer
a hadith in which the Prophet ﷺ reports Allah's words

hook.text: We recite Al-Fatihah at least 17 times a day. After mocks and a busy term, how can it stay fresh rather than automatic?
hook.a: By knowing Allah answers each ayah, pausing between ayat, and thinking about what we ask.

islamicLink.text: In a hadith qudsi reported by Muslim, Allah says He has divided the prayer between Himself and His servant: when the servant says 'Al-hamdu lillahi rabbil-'alamin', Allah says 'My servant has praised Me.'

quote.text: ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَلَمْ يَجْعَل لَّهُۥ عِوَجَا ۜ (١) قَيِّمًۭا لِّيُنذِرَ بَأْسًۭا شَدِيدًۭا مِّن لَّدُنْهُ وَيُبَشِّرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا حَسَنًۭا (٢) مَّٰكِثِينَ فِيهِ أَبَدًۭا (٣) وَيُنذِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوا۟ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ وَلَدًۭا (٤) مَّا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍۢ وَلَا لِءَابَآئِهِمْ ۚ كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةًۭ تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَٰهِهِمْ ۚ إِن يَقُولُونَ إِلَّا كَذِبًۭا (٥)

فَلَعَلَّكَ بَٰخِعٌۭ نَّفْسَكَ عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِمْ إِن لَّمْ يُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِهَٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ أَسَفًا (٦) إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا مَا عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ زِينَةًۭ لَّهَا لِنَبْلُوَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًۭا (٧) وَإِنَّا لَجَٰعِلُونَ مَا عَلَيْهَا صَعِيدًۭا جُرُزًا (٨) أَمْ حَسِبْتَ أَنَّ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْكَهْفِ وَٱلرَّقِيمِ كَانُوا۟ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَا عَجَبًا (٩) إِذْ أَوَى ٱلْفِتْيَةُ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ فَقَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةًۭ وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًۭا (١٠)
